## 1. Executive Summary

### Product Name & Tagline
**DirHub** - *Transform GitHub repositories into AI-powered documentation wikis*

### Purpose & Value Proposition
DirHub is a SaaS platform that automatically generates comprehensive, navigable documentation wikis for any GitHub repository using advanced AI analysis. It eliminates the manual burden of documentation while providing developers with instant, structured insights into codebases.

### Target Audience
- **Primary**: Development teams (5-50 developers) in tech companies
- **Secondary**: Individual developers, students, open-source maintainers
- **Tertiary**: Technical writers, DevOps engineers, software architects

### Expected Impact
- **Productivity**: Reduce onboarding time by 60-70%
- **Documentation**: Eliminate 80% of manual documentation effort
- **Code Comprehension**: Enable 3x faster codebase understanding
- **Collaboration**: Improve team knowledge sharing by 50%

---

## 2. Vision & Scope

### 3-5 Year Vision
Become the **de facto standard** for automated code documentation, powering documentation for 100,000+ repositories and serving 50,000+ development teams globally. Expand beyond GitHub to support GitLab, Bitbucket, and private enterprise repositories with advanced AI-powered code insights, semantic search, and collaborative documentation features.

### Product Mission
**Democratize code understanding** by making every repository instantly comprehensible through AI-generated, always-up-to-date documentation that developers actually want to use.

### In-Scope (Initial Phases)

#### Phase 1 - MVP (Weeks 1-8)
- ✅ GitHub repository processing (public repos)
- ✅ AI-powered wiki generation
- ✅ Basic search functionality
- ✅ Repository queue management
- ✅ Static wiki visualization

#### Phase 2 - Beta (Weeks 9-16)
- ✅ User authentication (GitHub OAuth)
- ✅ Private repository support
- ✅ Advanced search with filters
- ✅ Wiki version history
- ✅ Export functionality (PDF, Markdown)

#### Phase 3 - Growth (Weeks 17-24)
- ✅ Team collaboration features
- ✅ Custom documentation templates
- ✅ API access
- ✅ Webhook integrations
- ✅ Analytics dashboard

### Explicitly Out-of-Scope
- ❌ Code editing or IDE features
- ❌ Version control functionality (git operations)
- ❌ Code execution or testing
- ❌ Project management tools
- ❌ Real-time collaboration editing (Phase 1-2)
- ❌ Support for non-git repositories
- ❌ On-premise deployment (until Phase 4)

## 3. Problem & Solution

### Current Situation Analysis
Development teams face a **documentation crisis**:
- 62% of developers cite poor documentation as their biggest frustration (Stack Overflow Survey 2024)
- Teams spend 19.5 hours/week searching for code information
- Documentation becomes outdated within 2-3 weeks of creation
- New developers take 4-6 weeks to become productive on existing codebases

### Pain Points

#### User Pain Points
- **Time Waste**: Hours spent searching through code to understand functionality
- **Context Loss**: Difficulty understanding why code was written a certain way
- **Onboarding Hell**: New team members struggle to navigate unfamiliar codebases
- **Maintenance Burden**: Keeping documentation in sync with code is tedious

#### Business Pain Points
- **High Onboarding Costs**: $15,000-$30,000 per developer in lost productivity
- **Knowledge Silos**: Critical knowledge locked in senior developers' heads
- **Technical Debt**: Undocumented code becomes unmaintainable
- **Reduced Velocity**: Teams slow down as codebases grow

### Market Gap
**No existing solution combines**:
1. Automatic documentation generation from code
2. AI-powered semantic understanding
3. Always-up-to-date wiki format
4. Zero-effort maintenance
5. Developer-friendly UX

**Competitors**:
- **Confluence/Notion**: Manual documentation (outdated quickly)
- **Swagger/OpenAPI**: Only API documentation
- **Doxygen/JSDoc**: Technical reference, not narrative documentation
- **README generators**: Superficial, template-based

### Proposed Solution
**DirHub automatically**:
1. **Analyzes** repository structure, code, commits, and patterns using AI
2. **Generates** comprehensive wiki documentation with:
   - Architecture overview
   - File/folder explanations
   - Function/class documentation
   - Usage examples
   - Dependencies and relationships
3. **Organizes** information in navigable, searchable wiki format
4. **Updates** documentation automatically on repository changes

### Differentiation
| Feature | DirHub | Traditional Docs | Code Comments |
|---------|--------|------------------|---------------|
| **Auto-Generated** | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Always Current** | ✅ | ❌ | ⚠️ |
| **Narrative Format** | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ |
| **Zero Maintenance** | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
| **Semantic Search** | ✅ | ⚠️ | ❌ |
| **Visual Navigation** | ✅ | ⚠️ | ❌ |

## 5. User Stories

### Epic 1: Repository Discovery & Setup

**US-001**: Repository Search and Addition  
**As** Sarah (Senior Dev),  
**I want** to quickly add any GitHub repository to DirHub,  
**So that** I can get instant documentation without complex setup.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Can paste GitHub URL and submit
- [ ] System validates URL format
- [ ] Receives confirmation that repo is queued
- [ ] Process completes in < 5 minutes for typical repo
- [ ] Error messages are clear and actionable

**Technical Notes**: Support HTTPS and SSH GitHub URLs, handle rate limiting gracefully.

---

**US-002**: Repository Queue Monitoring  
**As** Alex (DevOps),  
**I want** to monitor processing status of multiple repositories,  
**So that** I know when documentation is ready.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Can view all queued repositories
- [ ] See real-time processing status (queued/processing/completed/failed)
- [ ] View estimated completion time
- [ ] Receive notification when processing completes
- [ ] Can re-process failed repositories

**Technical Notes**: Implement WebSocket or polling for real-time updates.

---

### Epic 2: Wiki Visualization & Navigation

**US-003**: Wiki Navigation  
**As** Marcus (Junior Dev),  
**I want** to navigate documentation like a wiki with folders and files,  
**So that** I can explore the codebase structure intuitively.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] See hierarchical folder/file tree
- [ ] Expand/collapse folders
- [ ] Click file to view documentation
- [ ] Breadcrumb navigation
- [ ] "Jump to file" quick navigation

**Technical Notes**: Use virtualized tree for large repos (1000+ files).

---

**US-004**: Code Documentation Display  
**As** Sarah (Senior Dev),  
**I want** to see AI-generated explanations for each file and function,  
**So that** my team can understand code without asking me.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Each file has summary explanation
- [ ] Functions/classes have individual documentation
- [ ] Code snippets with syntax highlighting
- [ ] Links to related files/functions
- [ ] "What changed" section showing recent updates

**Technical Notes**: Generate using GPT-4 or equivalent, cache results.

---

**US-005**: Advanced Search  
**As** Marcus (Junior Dev),  
**I want** to search across all documentation and code,  
**So that** I can find specific functionality quickly.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Full-text search across all content
- [ ] Search results show context (surrounding text)
- [ ] Filter by file type, folder, date
- [ ] Highlight search terms in results
- [ ] Jump directly to line in file

**Technical Notes**: Implement Elasticsearch or similar for performance.

---

### Epic 3: Collaboration & Sharing

**US-006**: Share Documentation  
**As** Sarah (Senior Dev),  
**I want** to share wiki links with my team,  
**So that** everyone has access to the same information.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Generate shareable link for specific wiki page
- [ ] Support public/private sharing modes
- [ ] Links work for authenticated users
- [ ] Can share specific file or section
- [ ] Preview shows repo name and file path

**Technical Notes**: Implement role-based access control.

---

**US-007**: Export Documentation  
**As** Alex (DevOps),  
**I want** to export wiki as PDF or Markdown,  
**So that** I can include it in compliance reports.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] Export full wiki to PDF
- [ ] Export to Markdown archive (zip)
- [ ] Maintain formatting and links
- [ ] Include table of contents
- [ ] Complete in < 30 seconds

**Technical Notes**: Use headless browser for PDF generation.

---

### Epic 4: User Account Management

**US-008**: GitHub Authentication  
**As** any user,  
**I want** to log in with my GitHub account,  
**So that** I can access private repositories.

**Acceptance Criteria**:
- [ ] OAuth login with GitHub
- [ ] Request minimal permissions initially
- [ ] Request private repo access on-demand
- [ ] Show connected account info
- [ ] Can disconnect/reconnect account

**Technical Notes**: Use GitHub OAuth Apps, store tokens securely.

---

## 6. Functional Requirements

### FR-1: Repository Processing
- **FR-1.1**: Support GitHub public repositories
- **FR-1.2**: Support GitHub private repositories (with OAuth)
- **FR-1.3**: Process repositories up to 10,000 files
- **FR-1.4**: Extract code structure (files, functions, classes)
- **FR-1.5**: Analyze commit history (last 100 commits)
- **FR-1.6**: Detect programming languages automatically
- **FR-1.7**: Parse README, CONTRIBUTING, LICENSE files

### FR-2: AI Documentation Generation
- **FR-2.1**: Generate repository overview (architecture, purpose)
- **FR-2.2**: Generate file-level documentation (what file does)
- **FR-2.3**: Generate function/class documentation
- **FR-2.4**: Extract and explain dependencies
- **FR-2.5**: Identify code patterns and best practices
- **FR-2.6**: Detect and document APIs/endpoints
- **FR-2.7**: Generate usage examples where applicable

### FR-3: Wiki Visualization
- **FR-3.1**: Display hierarchical folder/file tree
- **FR-3.2**: Collapsible/expandable folders
- **FR-3.3**: File content display with formatting
- **FR-3.4**: Syntax highlighting for code blocks
- **FR-3.5**: Markdown rendering for documentation
- **FR-3.6**: Breadcrumb navigation
- **FR-3.7**: Table of contents for long pages

### FR-4: Search Functionality
- **FR-4.1**: Full-text search across all content
- **FR-4.2**: Search filters (file type, folder, date)
- **FR-4.3**: Search result ranking by relevance
- **FR-4.4**: Search term highlighting
- **FR-4.5**: Search suggestions/autocomplete
- **FR-4.6**: Recent searches history

### FR-5: User Management
- **FR-5.1**: GitHub OAuth authentication
- **FR-5.2**: User profile management
- **FR-5.3**: Repository access control
- **FR-5.4**: Usage tracking and limits
- **FR-5.5**: Subscription plan management

### FR-6: Repository Management
- **FR-6.1**: Add new repository via URL
- **FR-6.2**: List user's repositories
- **FR-6.3**: Delete repository documentation
- **FR-6.4**: Re-process repository (refresh docs)
- **FR-6.5**: Repository status tracking
- **FR-6.6**: Processing queue management

---

## 7. Non-Functional Requirements

### NFR-1: Performance
- **NFR-1.1**: Repository processing < 5 minutes for repos with < 1000 files
- **NFR-1.2**: Wiki page load time < 2 seconds
- **NFR-1.3**: Search results return < 500ms
- **NFR-1.4**: Support 1000 concurrent users
- **NFR-1.5**: 99.5% uptime SLA

### NFR-2: Scalability
- **NFR-2.1**: Handle 10,000 repositories initially
- **NFR-2.2**: Scale to 100,000 repositories within 12 months
- **NFR-2.3**: Process 500 repositories/day
- **NFR-2.4**: Horizontal scaling for processing workers
- **NFR-2.5**: Database supports 1M+ documents

### NFR-3: Security
- **NFR-3.1**: HTTPS/TLS 1.3 for all connections
- **NFR-3.2**: OAuth tokens encrypted at rest
- **NFR-3.3**: Private repository data isolated per user
- **NFR-3.4**: Regular security audits (quarterly)
- **NFR-3.5**: OWASP Top 10 compliance
- **NFR-3.6**: Audit logging for all data access

### NFR-4: Compliance
- **NFR-4.1**: GDPR compliant (EU users)
- **NFR-4.2**: CCPA compliant (California users)
- **NFR-4.3**: SOC 2 Type II certification (within 18 months)
- **NFR-4.4**: Data retention policies documented
- **NFR-4.5**: Right to deletion (user data)

### NFR-5: Accessibility
- **NFR-5.1**: WCAG 2.1 AA compliance
- **NFR-5.2**: Keyboard navigation support
- **NFR-5.3**: Screen reader compatible
- **NFR-5.4**: Color contrast ratios meet standards
- **NFR-5.5**: Responsive design (mobile, tablet, desktop)

### NFR-6: Reliability
- **NFR-6.1**: Automated backups (daily)
- **NFR-6.2**: Disaster recovery plan (RPO < 24h, RTO < 4h)
- **NFR-6.3**: Error monitoring and alerting
- **NFR-6.4**: Graceful degradation on failures
- **NFR-6.5**: Rate limiting to prevent abuse

### NFR-7: Maintainability
- **NFR-7.1**: Code coverage > 80%
- **NFR-7.2**: Automated CI/CD pipeline
- **NFR-7.3**: Comprehensive API documentation
- **NFR-7.4**: Logging and monitoring integrated
- **NFR-7.5**: Database migrations versioned

## 8. Success Metrics

### Primary Metric (North Star)
**Active Documented Repositories**
- Definition: Repositories with at least 1 wiki view in last 30 days
- Target: 1,000 active repos by Month 6, 10,000 by Month 12
- Measurement: Database query, tracked daily

### Secondary Metrics

**User Engagement**
- **Wiki Views per User**: Target 50+ views/user/month
- **Search Queries**: Target 20+ searches/user/month
- **Session Duration**: Target 10+ minutes/session
- **Return Rate**: Target 60% weekly active users

**Business Metrics**
- **Monthly Recurring Revenue (MRR)**: $10K by Month 6, $50K by Month 12
- **Customer Acquisition Cost (CAC)**: < $100
- **Lifetime Value (LTV)**: > $500
- **Churn Rate**: < 5% monthly

**Product Quality**
- **Documentation Accuracy**: 85%+ (user feedback)
- **Processing Success Rate**: 95%+ (repos complete without errors)
- **Page Load Performance**: 90%+ pages < 2s
- **Search Relevance**: 80%+ queries find answer in top 5 results

**Adoption Metrics**
- **Time to First Wiki**: < 10 minutes from signup
- **Repositories per User**: 3+ average
- **Team Invite Rate**: 40% of users invite teammates
- **API Adoption**: 20% of power users use API by Month 12

### Measurement Timeline
- **Daily**: Active users, repositories processed, errors
- **Weekly**: Engagement metrics, performance metrics
- **Monthly**: Business metrics, churn, NPS
- **Quarterly**: Product quality surveys, user interviews

## 9. Roadmap

### Phase 1: MVP (Weeks 1-8) - "Make it Work"
**Goal**: Validate core value proposition with early adopters

**Scope**:

- ✅ Basic AI documentation generation
- ✅ Simple wiki visualization
- ✅ Basic search
- ✅ Queue management

**Success Criteria**:
- 100 users
- 500 repositories documented
- 70% user satisfaction (survey)
- Processing works for 90% of repos

**Timeline**: 8 weeks (2 sprints)

### Phase 2: Beta (Weeks 9-16) - "Make it Good"
**Goal**: Add essential features for broader adoption

**Scope**:
- ✅ GitHub OAuth authentication
- ✅ Private repository support
- ✅ Advanced search with filters
- ✅ Wiki version history
- ✅ Export functionality (PDF, Markdown)
- ✅ Improved AI documentation quality
- ✅ Mobile responsive design

**Success Criteria**:
- 500 users
- 2,500 repositories
- 75% user satisfaction
- < 5% processing failure rate

**Timeline**: 8 weeks (2 sprints)

---

### Phase 3: Growth (Weeks 17-24) - "Make it Scale"
**Goal**: Enable team collaboration and scaling

**Scope**:
- ✅ Team accounts and collaboration
- ✅ Custom documentation templates
- ✅ REST API for integrations
- ✅ Webhook support (auto-refresh)
- ✅ Analytics dashboard
- ✅ Role-based access control

**Success Criteria**:
- 2,000 users
- 10,000 repositories
- $10K MRR

**Timeline**: 8 weeks (2 sprints)

### Phase 4: Enterprise (Months 7-12) - "Make it Enterprise-Ready"
**Scope**:

**Target**: $50K MRR, 10,000+ users

## 10. Appendices

### A. Glossary
- **Wiki**: Structured documentation generated for a repository
- **Repository Processing**: Automated analysis and documentation generation
- **Queue**: FIFO system for managing repository processing jobs
- **AI Documentation**: LLM-generated explanations of code
- **Active Repository**: Repository with views in last 30 days

### B. Technical References
- GitHub REST API v3: https://docs.github.com/en/rest
- OpenAI GPT-4 API: https://platform.openai.com/docs
- Next.js App Router: https://nextjs.org/docs/app
- Radix UI Components: https://www.radix-ui.com

### C. Identified Risks

**Risk 1: AI Quality Inconsistency**
- **Severity**: High
- **Mitigation**: Human review loop, quality scoring, user feedback system
- **Owner**: Product Team

**Risk 2: GitHub API Rate Limits**
- **Severity**: Medium
- **Mitigation**: OAuth app with higher limits, caching, queue throttling
- **Owner**: Engineering Team

**Risk 3: Processing Cost (LLM APIs)**
- **Severity**: High
- **Mitigation**: Batch processing, caching, tiered pricing
- **Owner**: Engineering + Finance

**Risk 4: Repository Access Permissions**
- **Severity**: Medium
- **Mitigation**: Clear OAuth scopes, audit logging, access reviews
- **Owner**: Security Team

**Risk 5: Competitive Response**
- **Severity**: Low
- **Mitigation**: Fast execution, differentiated features, community building
- **Owner**: CEO

### D. External Dependencies
- **GitHub API**: Core dependency for repository access
- **OpenAI API**: AI documentation generation
- **Vercel/AWS**: Hosting and infrastructure
- **Stripe**: Payment processing
- **Auth0/NextAuth**: Authentication (alternative to custom OAuth)
